# Exercises for Part II {.unnumbered #sec-exercises-london}

These exercises collect Part II's hands-on work in order, one per checkpoint. Each names the
chapter that explains it, how you know you are done, and the line that catches you up if you
are not. A checkpoint is the state at the *end* of its block, so after catching up, skip to the
next exercise. Each checkpoint README also lists its steps, which work by hand; @sec-checkpoints
has the whole table.

Start the assistant in `~/london-guide/`, next to `~/quarto-workshop/`. Catching up reads
outside that folder, so approve the assistant's request to read `../quarto-workshop`.

## Exercise II.1: London in Markdown {.unnumbered}

From @sec-markdown. Write `london.md` with a heading, lists, a link, the Big Ben photo with alt
text and credit, a quotation, a table from `data/sights.csv` and a code fence; render it and keep
a live preview; write the project's `AGENTS.md`; give the folder its own environment with uv.

::: done
`london.html` shows both lists, the photo with its credit, the five-row table and the checklist,
and `uv run quarto check jupyter` reports the Python in this folder's `.venv`.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/01-london-markdown/README.md
```
:::

## Exercise II.2: a document that computes {.unnumbered}

From @sec-compute. Rename the guide to `london.qmd` with front matter, add a cell that reads
`data/attractions.csv` and a sentence with inline code, add a captioned, labelled bar chart, then
render to HTML, Word and a Typst PDF (and, optionally, PowerPoint, EPUB and Reveal.js).

::: done
`london.html` shows the title block, the computed sentence and a numbered chart, and
`london.docx` and `london.pdf` show the same sentence and chart.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/02-london-qmd/README.md
```
:::

## Exercise II.3: three audiences at once {.unnumbered}

From @sec-audiences. With one prompt and three sub-agents, write the dashboard, the Word brief
with its covering email, and the A5 flyer; the lead renders them one at a time.

::: done
`london-dashboard.html` has an Attractions page with three value boxes, a bar chart and a line
chart, and a Churches page listing ten churches with Visit London links; `london-email.docx`
opens with headings and working links; `london-email-message.md` holds the email in one text
block; `london-flyer.pdf` is one A5 page.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/04-london-audiences/README.md
```
:::

There is no checkpoint 03: the workshop's block numbering skips it.

## Exercise II.4: a published website {.unnumbered}

From @sec-publish. Make the folder a website with a navigation bar and a Downloads menu, put it
on GitHub, and publish it with an interactive `uv run quarto publish gh-pages`.

::: done
`https://<your-github-username>.github.io/london-guide/london-dashboard.html` opens on your phone.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/examples/london/README.md
```
:::

If you have already published, the catch-up copies the finished project's README over yours;
restore your own with `git checkout -- README.md`.

## Exercise II.5: change an input, explain the rebuild {.unnumbered}

From @sec-london-change, with no prompt supplied. Set the Tower of London's `visits_2025` to
`8000000`, predict which outputs change, rebuild, explain what changed and what did not, and
restore the real value with `git restore data/attractions.csv`.

::: done
you can name the outputs that changed, the ones that did not, and the line of code that links
each changed output to the input. Model answers are in @sec-checkpoints.
:::

## Going further {.unnumbered}

These build on Part II and have no checkpoints.

1. **Optional pieces.** Make the square advert (@sec-london-social), the white paper
   (@sec-london-whitepaper) or the three.js page (@sec-london-3d), if you skipped them.
2. **Turn a copy into a computation.** The flyer and the guide's table copy their facts from
   `data/sights.csv` (@tbl-london-deps). Ask the assistant to build the flyer's table from the
   file instead, then repeat Exercise II.5 with a change to a station name in `sights.csv`, and
   check that the flyer now follows. Restore the file afterwards.
3. **A map in two dimensions.** The 3-D map's data are in `data/places.csv` and the borough
   boundaries in `data/london-boroughs.geojson`. Ask for a third dashboard page that draws the
   sights and churches on a 2-D Plotly map from those files, with each point's source in its
   hover text.
4. **Update the live site.** After any change, ask the assistant to publish again with
   `uv run quarto publish gh-pages --no-prompt`, and check the change on your phone.
